name: Pangaea and the age of dinosaurs
life: No humans; reptiles, then dinosaurs dominate land
summary: Earth's continents were joined as Pangaea, which began splitting ~200 million years ago, setting the stage for today's map.
prompt: Photorealistic, scientifically accurate reconstruction of a Jurassic landscape on the supercontinent Pangaea with sauropod and theropod dinosaurs among cycads and conifers, volcanic horizon, documentary still, 16:9, no humans, no text

name: Age of mammals (Cenozoic)
life: Primates evolve; apes appear ~25 million years ago
summary: After the asteroid impact, mammals diversified; India collided with Asia, raising the Himalaya.
prompt: Photorealistic, scientifically accurate reconstruction of a Miocene grassland with early horses, ancient elephants and primitive apes at a forest edge, documentary still, 16:9, no humans, no text

name: Australopithecines
life: Upright walking apes living in small groups in woodland and savanna
summary: 'Lucy' (3.2 million years ago) walked upright with an ape-sized brain.
prompt: Photorealistic, scientifically accurate reconstruction of a small group of Australopithecus afarensis walking upright across an East African wooded savanna 3.2 million years ago, documentary still, 16:9, no text

name: Lower Paleolithic
life: Small mobile bands making stone tools; Homo erectus controls fire by ~1 million years ago
food: Scavenged and hunted meat, marrow, plants
species: Homo habilis, Homo erectus, mammoths, sabre-toothed cats
summary: The oldest stone tools (Lomekwi, 3.3 Mya) and Acheulean hand-axes; Homo erectus spread to Java and China. In India, Acheulean tools at Attirampakkam are ~1.5 million years old.

name: Middle Paleolithic
life: Homo sapiens appears in Africa (~300,000 years ago at Jebel Irhoud); Neanderthals in Europe bury dead and make jewellery
species: Neanderthals, Denisovans, Homo floresiensis, cave bears, woolly rhino
summary: Modern humans, Neanderthals and Denisovans coexisted and interbred; the Toba super-eruption (~74,000 years ago) blanketed India in ash.

name: Upper Paleolithic
life: Modern humans reach Australia (~65,000–50,000 years ago), Europe, Siberia and the Americas; cave art, needles, the bow
food: Mammoth, reindeer, horse, fish, wild plants
species: Woolly mammoth, cave lion, Irish elk, giant ground sloth, Megalania
summary: An explosion of art (Lascaux, Chauvet, Bhimbetka) during the last Ice Age; dogs domesticated from wolves.

name: Last Glacial Maximum
life: People retreat to refuges; sea level ~120 m lower; land bridges link Asia–America and Sri Lanka–India
summary: Ice sheets up to 3 km thick covered North America and northern Europe.

name: Mesolithic
life: Hunter-gatherers with microliths, canoes and semi-settled camps by lakes and coasts
summary: The world warmed after the Younger Dryas cold snap; megafauna went extinct; Göbekli Tepe's monumental temples (~9500 BCE) predate farming.

name: Neolithic Revolution
region: Fertile Crescent, China, Mesoamerica, Andes, New Guinea, Africa, South Asia
life: Settled villages, pottery, polished stone tools, herding
food: Wheat, barley, rice, millet, maize, lentils; goats, sheep, cattle, pigs
species: Domestic animals; aurochs (wild cattle) still roam
summary: Farming began independently in several regions; Çatalhöyük and Mehrgarh were among the first large villages.

name: Chalcolithic (Copper Age)
life: Copper tools alongside stone; first towns and long-distance trade; the wheel (~3500 BCE)
summary: Ötzi the Iceman (~3300 BCE) carried a copper axe; Indian Chalcolithic cultures (Ahar, Malwa, Jorwe).

name: Bronze Age
region: Near East, Egypt, Indus, China, Aegean
life: Cities, kings, writing, temples, armies, chariots
summary: Sumer, Egypt, the Indus civilisation and Shang China built the first states and writing systems.

name: 4.2-kiloyear event
life: Drought forces migrations and the collapse of cities
summary: A centuries-long dry spell linked to Akkad's fall, Egypt's First Intermediate Period and the de-urbanisation of the Indus cities.

name: Late Bronze Age collapse
life: Palaces burn; trade routes collapse; 'Sea Peoples' raid
summary: Mycenae, the Hittites and Ugarit fell within decades amid drought, earthquakes, invasions and systems failure.

name: Iron Age
life: Cheap iron tools and weapons; new kingdoms and alphabets
summary: Iron ploughs cleared the Ganga plain's forests, enabling the mahajanapadas; Phoenicians spread the alphabet.

name: Vedic period
life: Pastoral clans become kingdoms; Sanskrit hymns of the Rigveda; the varna system develops
summary: The Vedas, Upanishads and the 16 mahajanapadas emerge in the Ganga plain.

name: Axial Age
life: New philosophies and religions emphasising ethics and inner life
summary: Buddha, Mahavira, Confucius, Laozi, Socrates, Zoroastrian reform and Hebrew prophets reshaped thought.

name: Classical antiquity
life: City-states, democracy, philosophy, the Roman Empire
food: Bread, olive oil, wine, garum fish sauce
species: Lions and elephants captured for arenas
summary: Greece and Rome built the foundations of Western law, science and politics.

name: Mauryan and post-Mauryan India
life: A centralised empire, then regional kingdoms and Indo-Greek, Kushan and Satavahana trade states
summary: Ashoka's edicts promoted dhamma; Silk Road and Indian Ocean trade boomed.

name: Han and Roman era
life: Two vast empires linked by the Silk Road
summary: Paper was invented in Han China; Rome ruled ~70 million people.

name: Classical Golden Age of India (Gupta)
life: Flourishing art, mathematics (zero, decimal place value), astronomy and Sanskrit literature
summary: Aryabhata, Kalidasa, Nalanda University and Ajanta paintings.

name: Late Antique Little Ice Age
life: Cold summers, crop failures and plague
summary: Volcanic eruptions in 536, 540 and 547 caused one of the coldest decades in 2,000 years.

name: Early Middle Ages
life: Feudal lords, monasteries, Vikings; the rise of Islam
summary: Islam spread from Arabia to Spain and Sindh in a century.

name: Islamic Golden Age
life: Scholars translate Greek and Indian works; advances in algebra, optics, medicine
summary: Baghdad's House of Wisdom; al-Khwarizmi, Ibn Sina, Ibn al-Haytham.

name: Medieval Warm Period
life: Warmer summers; Vikings settle Greenland; population grows
summary: A regional warm spell, warmer in some places than others.

name: Chola and medieval India
life: Temple towns, naval expeditions, village assemblies
summary: The Cholas built Thanjavur's Brihadeeswara temple and raided Srivijaya.

name: Mongol era
life: The largest contiguous land empire links East and West
summary: Genghis Khan's empire spread trade, ideas — and plague.

name: Black Death era
life: Mass death, labour shortages, persecutions, end of serfdom in the West
summary: Killed perhaps 30–60% of Europe's population.

name: Little Ice Age
life: Frost fairs on the Thames, famines, glacier advances
summary: Cooler centuries linked to volcanoes and low solar activity.

name: Delhi Sultanate and Vijayanagara
life: Indo-Islamic architecture, Persian culture; a great Hindu empire in the south
summary: The Qutub Minar and Hampi's ruins are their monuments.

name: Renaissance
life: Revival of classical learning, art and science; the printing press
summary: Leonardo, Michelangelo, Gutenberg and Copernicus.

name: Age of Exploration
life: Ocean voyages; the Columbian Exchange
food: New World crops spread: maize, potato, chilli, tomato
species: Horses, cattle and smallpox reach the Americas
summary: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (1498); disease killed most of the Americas' Indigenous population.

name: Mughal era
life: Court culture, miniatures, Persian–Indian synthesis; India produces ~a quarter of world GDP around 1700
summary: Akbar's tolerance, the Taj Mahal and the decline after Aurangzeb.

name: Colonial era
life: European empires rule much of the world; plantations, the Atlantic slave trade
food: Sugar, tea, cotton, opium become global commodities
summary: The East India Company (1600) became ruler of India after Plassey (1757).

name: Scientific Revolution and Enlightenment
life: Experiment and reason challenge authority; revolutions in America and France
summary: Galileo, Newton, Locke, Voltaire.

name: Industrial Revolution
life: Factories, steam power, railways, cities; harsh child labour
summary: Coal-powered industry transformed work and began the rise in CO₂; India's textile industry was deindustrialised.

name: British Raj
life: Railways, telegraph, famines, nationalist movement
summary: Crown rule after 1857; the freedom struggle led by Gandhi, Nehru, Bose, Patel and many more ended in Independence and Partition.

name: World wars era
life: Total war, rationing, genocide, mass mobilisation
summary: Two world wars killed perhaps 85–100 million people.

name: Cold War
life: Nuclear standoff, decolonisation, space race
species: Laika and other animals in space
summary: The US and USSR competed without direct war; India led the Non-Aligned Movement.

name: Information Age
life: Computers, internet, smartphones, AI
summary: The internet connects ~5.5 billion people; AI transforms work.

name: Anthropocene
life: Human activity dominates Earth's systems
summary: A proposed epoch marked by plastics, nuclear fallout and rapid warming; formally rejected as an epoch in 2024 but widely used.
